title: Beyond connection: The challenge of expanding electricity access in Sub-Saharan Africa
gist: World Bank data blog (Atlas of Global Development 2026): 666 million people lacked electricity in 2023, 581 million in Sub-Saharan Africa where only about one in three rural residents has access; even connected households face poor reliability (Nigeria ~7 outages a week of ~12 hours), so access metrics must include reliability; Mission 300 targets 300 million Africans by 2030.

themes.theme: Access gap concentrated in Sub-Saharan Africa

insights.claim: In 2023, 666 million people worldwide lacked any electricity connection, 581 million of them in Sub-Saharan Africa.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: SSA is the overwhelming locus of unmet power demand, the core market for off-grid and grid expansion.
insights.quote: In 2023, 666 million people worldwide still lacked any connection to electricity.

insights.claim: In Sub-Saharan Africa only about one in three rural residents had electricity in 2023 versus more than four in five urban residents, reflecting high grid costs and low demand in sparse remote areas.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Rural SSA favors mini-grid and solar home system economics over grid extension.
insights.quote: only about one in three rural residents still had electricity in 2023, compared with more than four in five urban residents

insights.claim: Nigerian households report an average of nearly seven power outages in a seven-day period, each typically lasting about 12 hours, with similarly poor reliability in urban and rural areas.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Chronic unreliability sustains demand for generators, solar-plus-storage and distributed power in Nigeria.
insights.quote: households report an average of nearly seven power outages in a seven-day period, with each outage typically lasting about 12 hours
insights.locator: Even where households have a connection

insights.claim: Many households turn to diesel or petrol generators to keep essential services running, adding cost and pollution, so counting connections alone obscures service quality.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Generator displacement is an addressable market for distributed solar.
insights.locator: Many turn to diesel or petrol generators

insights.claim: Grid expansion remains important where cost-effective, but mini-grids and solar home systems can serve remote communities, and stronger utilities are needed for reliable supply.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Mixed grid/off-grid buildout and utility reform are the investable themes.

insights.claim: Mission 300, launched by the World Bank Group and the African Development Bank, aims to extend electricity access to 300 million people in Africa by 2030, which the authors say requires focus on dependable service, not just connection counts.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Large MDB-backed program creates deal flow in African power; watch reliability metrics.
